question: Why is it important for nurses to use standard nutritional terms?

options.A: It allows nurses to cook meals for patients.
options.B: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among the healthcare team.
options.C: It completely replaces the need for blood tests.
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge process.

explanation: Great job! Using clear, standard words means doctors, nurses, and dietitians are all on the same page, keeping your patients safe.

question: Why is drug distribution so important for a medication to work?

options.A: It stops the drug from binding to unwanted cells
options.B: It keeps the kidneys from filtering the drug out too fast
options.C: It ensures the drug reaches its specific target in the tissues
options.D: It converts inactive drugs into active chemicals

explanation: Medicines can't do much while just floating around in the blood vessels. They have to travel out into the tissues to lock onto their targets and help the patient heal.

question: Why must you report a needle-stick injury to your supervisor immediately?

options.A: To ensure the nurse receives disciplinary punishment for carelessness
options.B: To complete administrative paperwork for the hospital insurance policy
options.C: To replace the broken needle with a brand new syringe
options.D: To allow prompt medical evaluation and timely post-exposure prophylaxis

explanation: Spot on! Time matters with needle pricks. Getting quick medical advice and early preventive medication (PEP) keeps you safe.

question: What is the medical term for an abnormally enlarged spleen?

options.A: Hepatomegaly
options.B: Lymphadenopathy
options.C: Cardiomegaly
options.D: Splenomegaly

explanation: Splenomegaly means an enlarged spleen. You'll often see this when the spleen is overworked from filtering out abnormal blood cells.

question: What is the main reason nurses use a genogram?

options.A: To prescribe strong mental health drugs to relatives
options.B: To map out family relationships and health patterns across generations
options.C: To calculate the household's exact monthly salary
options.D: To check the caregiver's blood pressure

explanation: A genogram is basically a detailed family tree that helps you spot inherited health issues and relationship patterns at a single glance.

question: How is persistent depressive disorder different from major depressive disorder?

options.A: It affects only new mothers following childbirth
options.B: It only occurs during the winter months of the year
options.C: It is a chronic, milder form lasting for two years or longer
options.D: It lasts for exactly two weeks before disappearing entirely

explanation: Spot on! Persistent depressive disorder hangs around for a long time—two years or more—even if the daily symptoms are a bit milder than major depression.

question: An adult patient with dysphagia is getting ready to eat lunch. What is the best position for this patient?

options.A: Lying completely flat on their back
options.B: Lying on their side with knees bent
options.C: Reclining at a comfortable 30-degree angle
options.D: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle

explanation: An upright posture uses gravity to help food move safely down the esophagus instead of entering the airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h6)

question: A digital monitor shows a very high blood pressure for a calm patient who feels totally fine. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Write down the machine's number and walk away to another room
options.B: Check the reading manually using a stethoscope and manual cuff
options.C: Rush to give the patient strong blood pressure-lowering drugs
options.D: Throw the electronic device away and never use it again

explanation: Machines can glitch! If a result doesn't match how the patient looks or feels, always double-check it manually before panicking or treating.

question: How does cyanide primarily cause damage inside human cells?

options.A: It binds permanently to calcium channels in cardiac muscle tissue.
options.B: It directly dissolves the lipid bilayer of red blood cells.
options.C: It triggers widespread liquefactive necrosis in the esophagus.
options.D: It inhibits mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase, halting cellular respiration.

explanation: Cyanide attacks the powerhouses of our cells (the mitochondria). By blocking cytochrome c oxidase, cells can no longer use oxygen to make energy, leading to rapid collapse.

question: A woman who delivered a healthy baby six hours ago starts bleeding heavily, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.B: Leave the ward to call the senior consultant doctor immediately
options.C: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.D: Massage the uterus gently to stimulate contraction and expel clots

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus after delivery indicates uterine atony, which requires immediate fundal massage to stimulate contraction and reduce bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: What actually drives water to move passively across the wall of the intestine?

options.A: Active water pumps on the enterocyte membrane
options.B: Changes in core body temperature
options.C: Direct muscle contractions of the villi
options.D: Osmotic gradients created by solute absorption

explanation: Water loves to follow the crowd! As the gut pumps in salts and sugars, water naturally flows right along with them through osmosis.

question: Which part of the early blastocyst grows to become the baby's side of the placenta?

options.A: Amniotic cavity
options.B: Zona pellucida
options.C: Trophoblast
options.D: Inner cell mass

explanation: You've got this! The outer layer, called the trophoblast, reaches out to connect with the mother's uterine lining to form the placenta.

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to check a pregnant patient's diet early on?

options.A: It determines the exact date of conception
options.B: It replaces the need for standard laboratory blood tests
options.C: It allows for the early identification and correction of nutrient deficits
options.D: It stops gestational diabetes from ever developing

explanation: Spotting nutritional gaps early helps you stop issues like tiredness or baby growth delays before they become serious. Great nursing insight!

question: What are the classic signs that a patient has developed a post-abortion pelvic infection?

options.A: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever
options.B: Clear, watery discharge lasting several days
options.C: Sudden painless swelling of the lower limbs
options.D: High blood pressure and severe throbbing headache

explanation: Spot on! Bad-smelling discharge and fever are major warning signs that bacteria have entered the uterus.

question: What is meant by the 'utilization rate' of a healthcare facility?

options.A: How quickly the pharmacy dispenses routine medications
options.B: The total number of chairs in the hospital waiting room
options.C: The monthly electricity bill paid by the clinic
options.D: How often community members actually visit and use the services

explanation: Utilization rate measures the extent to which the target population uses available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: A nurse and a social worker disagree on how to discharge an elderly patient who lives alone. What should guide their next step?

options.A: Following the nurse's plan because nurses spend more time at the bedside
options.B: Letting the patient leave without any support services
options.C: Focusing on the patient's needs through shared decision-making
options.D: Escalating the disagreement to the hospital director immediately

explanation: Exactly! When team members see things differently, putting the patient's welfare first and talking it through always points the way forward.

question: How can a nurse best handle personal biases when caring for a stigmatized patient?

options.A: Reading legal textbooks to punish patients who break social norms
options.B: Asking another nurse to handle all female reproductive health cases
options.C: Practicing active self-reflection and discussing feelings with supportive peers
options.D: Suppressing all emotions until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Talking things through with supportive colleagues and checking your own mindset helps you catch hidden biases before they affect your patient care.

question: Which medication class is widely known to cause constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Short-acting diuretics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Opioids slow down gastrointestinal motility significantly, which frequently leads to stubborn constipation in patients taking them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: In the early days following Nightingale's work, what was the main focus of nursing studies?

options.A: Advanced surgical interventions
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug development
options.C: Hospital financial management
options.D: Nursing education and training methods

explanation: Spot on! Before diving heavily into clinical care, early nurse researchers first wanted to figure out the best ways to train and educate nurses.

question: Which pain scale uses cartoon faces ranging from a happy smile to a crying face?

options.A: Behavioral Pain Scale
options.B: Visual Analog Scale
options.C: Wong-Baker FACES Scale
options.D: Numeric Rating Scale

explanation: The Wong-Baker FACES scale uses friendly facial drawings, making it super helpful for children or patients who struggle to use numbers.

question: What makes blunt force trauma to the abdomen so dangerous?

options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key!

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between compressions?

options.A: It keeps the electrical conduction system stable
options.B: It gives the rescuer a chance to rest their arms
options.C: It allows the heart chambers to refill with blood
options.D: It prevents broken ribs in older adults

explanation: Without full chest recoil, the heart stays partly squeezed and cannot fill properly for the next push. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h2)

question: An 85-year-old retired civil servant comes to the clinic with joint pain and feeling very lonely. Which government program can help with both issues?

options.A: Giving them a heavy-duty vehicle driving license
options.B: Enrolling them in mandatory military training
options.C: Sending them to a full-time industrial workshop
options.D: Geriatric care integration and social protection programs

explanation: Great choice! Specialized geriatric care treats their physical aches, while social programs step in to beat loneliness and build community connection.

question: How often should you check vital signs during the first two hours after delivery?

options.A: Every hour
options.B: Every 4 hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Spot on! Checking vitals every fifteen minutes right after delivery helps us catch sudden bleeding or shock super early, keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: Why are some STIs tricky because they don't show any physical signs or symptoms?

options.A: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they have it
options.B: Laboratory tests cannot detect pathogens if symptoms are absent
options.C: The body builds permanent immunity during the latent phase
options.D: Asymptomatic infections always resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Exactly! When someone has no symptoms, they feel healthy and can unknowingly pass the infection to their partners. Good thinking!

question: A patient asks why taking gym steroids can cause infertility. How should you explain it?

options.A: Testosterone supplements cause the blood-testis barrier to permanently close off blood supply
options.B: External hormones trick the brain into stopping natural LH and FSH production, which shuts down sperm creation in the testes
options.C: High hormone levels cause the prostate gland to block the urethra completely
options.D: Anabolic steroids directly dissolve mature sperm stored inside the epididymis and vas deferens

explanation: When you put artificial testosterone into the body, the brain thinks, 'We have too much!' and stops making the hormones (LH and FSH) that tell the testes to make sperm.

question: How do governments use healthcare spending as a percentage of GDP?

options.A: To calculate individual patient prescription costs
options.B: To set the daily working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To determine the required passing grade for nursing students
options.D: To measure how much national wealth goes toward medical care

explanation: This ratio shows the proportion of a country's total economic output dedicated to keeping people healthy and running health services.

question: Why is planning essential for a nursing unit?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for daily staff evaluations
options.B: It prevents chaos and ensures efficient use of resources
options.C: It allows nurses to bypass hospital policies during emergencies
options.D: It ensures that doctors do all the administrative work

explanation: A solid plan helps nurse managers anticipate needs, allocate staff properly, and keep patient care organized and safe. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h1)

question: Unlike hospital nursing which looks after one patient at a time, what is the main focus of community health nursing?

options.A: The health of entire populations and communities
options.B: Critical care management in intensive units
options.C: Laboratory testing and biomedical research
options.D: Surgical interventions and post-operative recovery

explanation: Spot on! While hospital nurses care for individual bedside patients, community nurses look at the bigger picture—the health needs of whole neighborhoods and populations.

question: A patient lacks a specific nutrient in their diet and shows deficiency signs, but labs show their body can easily make similar compounds. What kind of nutrient is this?

options.A: Inorganic mineral
options.B: Essential nutrient
options.C: Inert fiber
options.D: Non-essential nutrient

explanation: If the body can synthesize it independently, it's considered non-essential because we don't strictly have to get it directly from our meals.

question: A nurse deliberately skips the standard bedside check before giving medication just because they are feeling lazy. How should this be handled in a Just Culture?

options.A: Retrain the entire nursing department immediately
options.B: Blame the hospital management for poor equipment
options.C: Ignore the incident because humans make mistakes
options.D: Hold the nurse accountable for reckless behavior

explanation: Spot on! Honest mistakes get support and system fixes, but choosing to break safety rules out of laziness is reckless and requires individual accountability.

question: Where are our actual smell (olfactory) receptor cells located?

options.A: Inside the hard palate of the mouth
options.B: On the roof of the nasal cavity
options.C: Along the lower respiratory tract
options.D: Within the external ear canal

explanation: Spot on! The delicate olfactory epithelium holding our smell receptors sits high up near the roof of the nasal cavity, right where incoming air sweeps past.

question: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) happens when there is an overgrowth of which specific organism?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: You got it! Gardnerella vaginalis and other anaerobic bacteria multiply too much in BV, pushing out our helpful flora. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: A patient has a viral cough and cold. Why won't standard antibiotics help clear it up?

options.A: Viruses multiply too slowly for antibiotics to catch them in time
options.B: Viral agents are too large to be penetrated by oral medications
options.C: Antibiotics immediately destroy the white blood cells fighting the virus
options.D: Viruses lack the cellular structures that standard antibacterial drugs target

explanation: Antibiotics are built to attack bacteria (like destroying their cell walls). Since viruses are structured differently, antibiotics just can't touch them!

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward
options.B: Purchasing heavy-duty earthquake-resistant generators
options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

explanation: That's right! Laws and policies are non-structural measures that guide us away from dangerous areas without physical building changes.

question: Which type of precautions must you use for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Standard Precautions
options.B: Airborne Precautions
options.C: Reverse Isolation
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: Spot on! Standard Precautions are our trusty baseline defense for every patient encounter because we never know an infection's status right away.

question: Which type of facility usually provides secondary level healthcare services?

options.A: General hospitals
options.B: Teaching hospitals
options.C: Traditional herbal shops
options.D: Primary health centres

explanation: Well done! General hospitals step in when patients need doctors who specialize in specific areas, minor surgeries, or admission beyond what a primary health center can handle.

question: The legal term 'respondeat superior' is often used in court. What does it translate to in English?

options.A: First do no harm
options.B: To err is human
options.C: Let the master answer
options.D: The facts speak for themselves

explanation: It's an old Latin phrase meaning 'let the master answer'—meaning the boss (the hospital) answers for the worker's actions.

question: What triggers an outbreak investigation in a healthcare facility?

options.A: An unusual cluster of infections detected by surveillance
options.B: A routine check of fire extinguishers
options.C: The arrival of a new hospital director
options.D: The annual painting of the ward walls

explanation: Surveillance spots the abnormal rise in cases, which prompts a full investigation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to respond when a client shares a traditional belief that goes against medical science?

options.A: Argue aggressively until the client agrees to abandon their tradition
options.B: Scold the client publicly to discourage others from holding similar views
options.C: Listen patiently and gently provide accurate health education without mockery
options.D: Ignore the client and refuse to provide any further medical care

explanation: Spot on! Respectful listening builds trust, making the client much more willing to listen to your advice.

question: Why are nurses considered frontline workers in infection surveillance?

options.A: They spend the most time observing patients at the bedside
options.B: They design the computer software used for hospital records
options.C: They are the only staff allowed to write public health laws
options.D: They fund all the laboratory testing in the facility

explanation: Bedside presence allows nurses to spot early signs of infection before anyone else. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why do surgeons place a surgical drain inside a wound after an operation?

options.A: To keep the patient completely immobile during recovery
options.B: To prevent fluid and blood from collecting inside the wound
options.C: To deliver strong liquid antibiotics directly into tissues
options.D: To speed up the healing of skin stitches

explanation: You've got this! Drains are simply there to stop blood or serum from forming nasty pockets that could lead to an infection. Great clinical thinking!

question: You just finished giving an elderly patient a bed bath. How should you dry their skin safely?

options.A: Rub their skin hard to wake up blood flow
options.B: Pat the skin dry gently with a soft towel
options.C: Put thick lotion tightly between their toes
options.D: Use a hair dryer on high heat to dry them quickly

explanation: Spot on! Older skin is quite fragile. Always pat gently with a soft towel instead of scrubbing, which can tear the skin.

question: What is the standard lab test used to check for urinary schistosomiasis?

options.A: Blood culture to isolate active bacterial colonies
options.B: Urine microscopy using filtration to find eggs
options.C: Chest X-ray to visualize lung calcifications
options.D: Liver biopsy to inspect adult worm clusters

explanation: By filtering a urine sample, lab technicians can catch the tiny parasite eggs under a microscope. Simple, non-invasive, and effective!

question: Which physical assessment step must a nurse ALWAYS do before pressing on a patient's abdomen?

options.A: Percussion
options.B: Palpation
options.C: Auscultation
options.D: Inspection

explanation: Awesome clinical thinking! Always listen with your stethoscope first so you don't accidentally alter natural bowel sounds by pressing on the tummy.

question: Why is meeting the deadline for monthly health reports so important for a health clinic?

options.A: It allows nurses to take mandatory annual leave.
options.B: It ensures district and national health authorities can track trends and distribute resources without delay.
options.C: It guarantees free medical equipment from foreign donors.
options.D: It stops patients from visiting during the first week of the new month.

explanation: On-time reports help the whole health system run smoothly so districts know where supplies and support need to go next.

question: Why is it always smart to let a friend read your draft before you submit it?

options.A: It guarantees that your study will receive immediate funding
options.B: Writers often become blind to their own typographical and logical errors
options.C: Colleagues are legally required to rewrite the entire document for you
options.D: Peer review replaces the need for a formal methodology section

explanation: When you've stared at a paper for hours, typos hide from you! A fresh pair of eyes can spot little mistakes in seconds.

question: How does keeping a patient close to your body help protect your back during a transfer?

options.A: It reduces the physical load and leverage on your spine
options.B: It makes the patient feel much safer and calmer
options.C: It prevents the patient from falling forward
options.D: It allows you to finish the hospital shift faster

explanation: Keeping heavy objects close to your center of gravity decreases the strain placed on your lower back muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h3)

question: Which group of viruses is most commonly spread through contaminated injection equipment?

options.A: Respiratory viruses like Influenza and the common cold
options.B: Fungal spores that cause superficial skin rashes
options.C: Intestinal parasites spread through contaminated water
options.D: Blood-borne pathogens like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Because unsafe injections often transfer tiny amounts of blood between people, blood-borne viruses are our biggest concern in clinical safety.

question: Why is community education just as important as legal bans when fighting to eliminate FGM?

options.A: Healthcare workers are not allowed to read legal documents
options.B: Community education changes cultural beliefs and tackles the root causes
options.C: Community leaders demand payment to obey the law
options.D: Laws are too expensive to print and distribute

explanation: You got it! While laws set the rules, stopping deep-seated traditions requires educating community members so they choose to leave the practice behind. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when giving IV fluids or blood products?

options.A: Patients always feel severe pain when any fluid enters a vein
options.B: Every procedure carries inherent risks such as fluid overload or severe reactions
options.C: Intravenous lines are guaranteed to clog within one hour
options.D: Hospital management requires extra paperwork for all fluid bags

explanation: Even though giving fluids is an everyday task, putting anything straight into the bloodstream can cause rapid changes or reactions. Staying alert keeps our patients safe!

question: What two main things interact during a serological test to confirm a microbe is present?

options.A: Peptidoglycan and crystal violet
options.B: Agar and nutrient broth
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide and catalase
options.D: Antigens and antibodies

explanation: You got it! Serology relies on the precise lock-and-key fit between the germ's antigens and our body's antibodies.

question: What makes the measuring tape especially useful for community health nursing?

options.A: It can diagnose complex infectious diseases
options.B: It is portable, cheap, and non-invasive
options.C: It provides automated digital health records
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: Field tools must be easy to carry and simple to use without hurting the patient, making basic tape measures ideal for outreach work. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which nursing action is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries and must be avoided?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands
options.B: Wearing clean gloves during procedures
options.C: Using single-dose medication vials
options.D: Performing hand hygiene before patient contact

explanation: Recapping used needles is a dangerous habit that frequently leads to accidental finger pricks. Keep safety first and drop them straight into the bin!

question: Why do theatres carefully monitor room temperature and humidity during surgery?

options.A: To make the room comfortable for visitors and family members
options.B: To ensure surgical instruments do not rust during the procedure
options.C: To discourage bacterial growth and prevent patient hypothermia
options.D: To keep the anesthesia machine running at peak efficiency

explanation: Controlling the climate stops bacteria from multiplying and protects the patient's body heat while they are under anesthesia. You've got this!

question: Which hormone helps your kidneys save water when your body is dehydrated?

options.A: Anti-diuretic hormone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Think of Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) as your body's 'anti-pee' signal. It tells your kidney collecting ducts to hold onto water so you don't get dehydrated.

question: A clinic nurse tests a urine sample from a 32-week pregnant woman and finds protein in it. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Gestational hypertension with pre-eclampsia
options.B: Normal physiological kidney adaptation
options.C: Severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Dietary sugar overload from lunch

explanation: Protein in the urine combined with high blood pressure later in pregnancy is a classic warning sign of pre-eclampsia that needs immediate attention.

question: Why do healthcare workers usually resist new changes in the workplace?

options.A: Laziness and a general refusal to work hard
options.B: A normal defense mechanism against the unknown
options.C: An inadequate level of basic clinical training
options.D: A deliberate attempt to sabotage patient safety

explanation: You're doing great! Resistance isn't about being lazy—it's just a natural human reaction when our daily routine gets shaken up by the unknown.

question: When you help a patient improve their nutrition knowledge, what practical skill does it usually help them master?

options.A: Surgical techniques for weight loss
options.B: Hospital administrative policies
options.C: Food labels and portion sizes
options.D: Pharmaceutical drug interactions

explanation: You got it! Boosting health literacy means helping patients decode food packages and understand serving sizes so they can take charge of their plates.

question: Which part of the chain of infection do standard precautions target the most?

options.A: The mode of transmission
options.B: The susceptible host
options.C: The microbial reservoir
options.D: The infectious agent itself

explanation: You got it! Barriers like gloves, masks, and hand hygiene cut off the travel route, stopping pathogens from moving from the source to the patient or nurse.

question: What makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care (EmONC) center different from a basic one?

options.A: The ability to perform blood transfusions and Caesarean sections
options.B: The presence of pediatricians in the delivery room at all times
options.C: The requirement that mothers stay in the hospital for a full month
options.D: The exclusive use of traditional herbal remedies for pain

explanation: When things get tough, a comprehensive center can handle surgeries like C-sections and give blood transfusions—things basic clinics can't do. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: What special chemical is added to the blood collection tube for a fasting blood sugar test to keep the blood cells from eating up the sugar?

options.A: Potassium EDTA
options.B: Sodium fluoride
options.C: Heparin sulfate
options.D: Calcium chloride

explanation: Great job! Sodium fluoride acts as a preservative (glycolytic inhibitor) that stops red blood cells from consuming the glucose in the tube before the lab technician can test it.

question: According to the Spaulding classification, what level of processing is required for surgical instruments?

options.A: Basic washing with soap
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: Surgical instruments are classified as critical items because they enter sterile tissues, so they must be fully sterilized. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What term describes the final coming together of the male and female genetic material (chromosomes)?

options.A: Ovulation
options.B: Capacitation
options.C: Syngamy
options.D: Atresia

explanation: Syngamy is the exact moment the chromosomes from mum and dad finally mix together to form the unique genetic blueprint of the new baby.

question: Which of the following describes a key difference between screening tests and diagnostic tests in prenatal care?

options.A: Screening tests estimate risk, while diagnostic tests confirm a condition
options.B: Diagnostic tests are performed on every single pregnant woman
options.C: Screening tests are only done after birth
options.D: Screening tests use surgery, while diagnostic tests are painless

explanation: Screening tests only show the probability or risk of a disorder, whereas diagnostic tests provide a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: A patient had a right-sided mastectomy last year. Which arm should you use for venepuncture?

options.A: On the right arm
options.B: On the left arm
options.C: In the right hand veins only
options.D: Either arm without preference

explanation: Always avoid the arm on the side of a previous mastectomy because lymph flow there is compromised, making infections much harder to fight off.

question: When is the best time to check the psychosocial needs of a patient with a chronic blood disorder?

options.A: Exclusively on the first day of the initial hospital visit
options.B: Whenever the patient requests a change in their medication
options.C: As an ongoing process throughout the course of the illness
options.D: Only during the final stage of palliative care admission

explanation: A patient's worries change as their illness progresses. Checking in regularly lets you catch new stress early!

question: What is the primary purpose of an antibiotic stewardship program in a hospital?

options.A: Ensuring the hospital pharmacy always has the most expensive drugs
options.B: Promoting the correct and prudent use of antibiotics to fight resistance
options.C: Banning the use of all injectable medications in outpatient clinics
options.D: Lowering the academic qualifications required for hospital prescribers

explanation: Antibiotic stewardship programs optimize antimicrobial use to preserve their effectiveness and curb resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)

question: What does cross-contamination mean in food safety?

options.A: The accidental freezing of fresh vegetables in the refrigerator
options.B: The mixing of two different dry grains in the same storage bin
options.C: The transfer of harmful germs from raw food to ready-to-eat food
options.D: The change in food color due to exposure to bright sunlight

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when bacteria move from raw items (like meat) to food you're about to eat without cooking.

question: A family tells their young boy not to cry because 'boys must be strong.' What does this show?

options.A: A congenital developmental delay
options.B: A normal physiological reflex
options.C: An innate hormonal imbalance
options.D: The transmission of gender norms

explanation: You nailed it! Families and communities pass down gender expectations every day by teaching children how they 'should' express their feelings.

question: Why are notifiable disease registers important for public health authorities?

options.A: They calculate the monthly salary of hospital staff
options.B: They track legally reportable infections to protect the public
options.C: They replace the need for patient physical examinations
options.D: They determine which patients get discharged first

explanation: Registers keep a formal record of dangerous infections that require immediate public health action. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the main goal of community nursing advocacy for smoke-free indoor public spaces?

options.A: To protect non-smokers and children from the dangers of secondhand smoke
options.B: To help current smokers reduce their daily cigarette count
options.C: To reduce the government spending on imported medical supplies
options.D: To eliminate all tobacco farming in rural agricultural areas

explanation: Smoke-free rules ensure that people who don't smoke aren't forced to breathe in harmful tobacco smoke. Amazing job completing this session!

question: What is the 'Hawthorne effect' in a research study?

options.A: The sudden drop in blood pressure caused by new drugs
options.B: Alteration of behavior by subjects who know they are being observed
options.C: A permanent loss of study participants over time
options.D: The financial cost of running a large hospital trial

explanation: Correct! People naturally change how they act when they know someone is watching them, which can sometimes trick our research findings.

question: Why is it smart for nurse managers to review staff feedback surveys about teamwork and collaboration?

options.A: To identify departmental friction points before they cause patient harm
options.B: To replace all human staff members with automated software
options.C: To decide which staff members deserve a pay cut
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future meetings

explanation: You got it! Surveys give the team a voice to point out where things are clashing, allowing managers to step in and fix things proactively.

question: Which clinical sign is a classic indicator of respiratory distress in a newborn?

options.A: Strong, rhythmic sucking reflexes
options.B: Regular, deep, quiet breathing
options.C: A pink, warm skin appearance
options.D: Intercostal chest retractions

question: A nurse researcher wants to study patient hygiene habits in a ward without changing their routine. What is the most suitable data collection approach?

options.A: A laboratory test
options.B: A clinical drug trial
options.C: Surgical intervention
options.D: Direct observation

explanation: To see how people naturally behave without them putting on an act, direct observation in their real environment works best. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: When caring for a patient with a sensory impairment, what should a community health nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without teaching them anything
options.B: Insist that the patient pay double for clinic registration
options.C: Advocate for accessible communication tools like braille or interpreters
options.D: Assume the patient cannot understand basic instructions

question: Why do germs love growing in fresh milk?

options.A: It is completely sterile when it leaves the udder
options.B: It lacks water molecules necessary for bacterial life
options.C: It contains rich nutrients and a nearly neutral pH
options.D: It has a high acid content that preserves the liquid

explanation: You've got this! Milk is packed with water, proteins, fats, and sugar (lactose) at a nearly neutral pH, which makes it a dream home for bacteria to multiply rapidly.

question: Why is writing down clear, objective notes on a client's nutrition progress so important?

options.A: It ensures clear communication among the healthcare team over time
options.B: It replaces the need to talk directly with the client
options.C: It fulfills legal requirements to discharge the patient immediately
options.D: It guarantees the client will never experience health issues again

explanation: Spot on! Good documentation helps every nurse and doctor on the team track what's working and adjust care smoothly.

question: Why might two patients who had the exact same surgery report completely different pain levels?

options.A: One patient is always just exaggerating their discomfort
options.B: Hospital room temperatures change how nerves send distress signals
options.C: Surgical skill varies so much that tissue injury is never identical
options.D: Pain involves emotional and cultural factors, not just physical injury

explanation: Spot on! Pain isn't just about the physical cut. A person's emotions, background, and past experiences all change how they feel and express pain.

question: How does scarcity directly affect your daily life as a nurse on the ward?

options.A: It forces nurses to prioritize care and manage limited supplies efficiently
options.B: It requires nurses to personally fund ward equipment purchases
options.C: It automatically lowers the quality of medications available in pharmacies
options.D: It prevents hospitals from ever admitting emergency trauma patients

explanation: Spot on! Because time and gloves are never endless, great nurses learn to prioritize and manage what they have to keep every patient safe. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which lifestyle change is a major reason diabetes is becoming more common in Nigerian cities?

options.A: Engaging in heavy manual farm labor every morning
options.B: Consuming excessive amounts of natural spring water
options.C: Increasing daily intake of green leafy vegetables
options.D: Adopting processed diets and reducing physical activity

explanation: With busy city life, more people eat fast, processed foods and move around less. This shift in lifestyle greatly increases metabolic risks. Great insight for community nursing!

question: A mother exclusively breastfeeding her four-month-old baby notices her monthly period just returned. What should you advise her about LAM?

options.A: Her body is just adjusting and she is still fully protected from pregnancy
options.B: She should stop breastfeeding immediately to restore protection
options.C: She can continue relying on LAM safely until the baby is one year old
options.D: LAM is no longer reliable, and she should add another family planning method

explanation: The return of her monthly period means her body's fertility cycle has woken back up. Time to introduce a backup family planning method!

question: An elderly patient loses sensation in their feet due to nerve issues. Which systems must they rely on most to stay balanced?

options.A: Cutaneous touch receptors
options.B: Vestibular and visual systems
options.C: Proprioceptive joint sensors
options.D: Chemical blood pressure sensors

explanation: When the feet can't feel the ground well, the patient has to depend heavily on their inner ears and eyesight to stay steady. Good clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which of these nursing duties counts as a skilled nursing intervention?

options.A: Managing complex wound care and dressing changes.
options.B: Assisting a resident with walking down the hallway.
options.C: Handing out meal trays to all residents at lunchtime.
options.D: Helping a resident put on their casual daytime clothes.

explanation: Wound care needs professional clinical technique and assessment, making it a true skilled nursing task!

question: Why can taking very large megadoses of fat-soluble vitamins be dangerous?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in the body and can accumulate to toxic levels
options.B: The body attacks fat-soluble vitamins as foreign bacteria and triggers shock
options.C: Excess fat-soluble vitamins instantly turn into dangerous trans fats
options.D: High doses immediately cause total kidney failure by dissolving water in blood

explanation: Spot on! Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in our body fat and liver instead of being peed out, taking too many over time can build up to dangerous levels.

question: What is a major benefit of working with a mobilized community for a nurse?

options.A: Health messages spread easily through local networks
options.B: All diseases are completely eradicated overnight
options.C: Nurses no longer need to write patient records
options.D: The government stops paying salaries to health workers

explanation: When a community is mobilized, people talk to each other about health, making health education spread fast. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h3)

question: What happens when communication breaks down during a disaster response?

options.A: The federal government automatically increases funding for local clinics
options.B: International aid organizations decide to withdraw completely from the region
options.C: Rescue efforts stall and resources are wasted due to lack of coordination
options.D: Community members become more resilient against future emergencies

explanation: Good communication is everything! Without it, teams duplicate work or miss sending help to where it's needed most.

question: Why might a patient with salpingitis feel deep pelvic pain during sexual intercourse?

options.B: Hormonal shifts completely stop natural vaginal lubrication
options.C: Pelvic thrusting puts pressure on inflamed, swollen fallopian tubes and surrounding tissues
options.D: The infection causes immediate dryness of the external labial skin

question: What is the medical term for the excessive thirst that a diabetic patient often feels?

options.A: Polyphagia
options.B: Polyuria
options.C: Polydipsia
options.D: Paresthesia

question: When does a health situation officially become an epidemic?

options.A: When case numbers suddenly rise above the normal expected baseline
options.B: When the causative organism is a drug-resistant bacteria
options.C: When it spreads to at least three different continents
options.D: When hospitals run out of basic treatment medications

explanation: You've got this! An epidemic happens when there is an unusual surge of cases in a community—basically, way more people falling sick than what healthcare workers normally expect to see.

question: What is the main reason for teaching pregnant women about pregnancy danger signs right in their homes?

options.A: To frighten them into staying indoors
options.B: To reduce the number of required antenatal visits
options.C: To ensure they recognize complications early and seek prompt help
options.D: To test their memory during clinic visits

explanation: When mums and families know what warning signs look like (like heavy bleeding or severe headaches), they act fast before things get dangerous.

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

question: Why is it important that junior health workers feel comfortable speaking up about safety concerns?

options.A: Every team member can spot errors and protect patient safety
options.B: It speeds up staff promotion processes in the clinic

options.D: It allows junior staff to take over the doctor's duties

question: When would a nurse researcher decide to use a non-experimental design?

options.A: When ethical reasons prevent assigning patients to a harmful exposure
options.B: When proving that a specific nursing intervention directly causes a cure
options.C: When testing the exact dosage of a brand new surgical medication
options.D: When controlling every environmental factor in a hospital room

explanation: Spot on! Sometimes it is just plain wrong or unethical to expose people to risk on purpose (like smoking or harmful substances), so we use non-experimental designs to study them safely.

question: A 17-year-old girl is worried she will forget to take a daily pill. Which contraceptive option fits her lifestyle best?

options.A: Subdermal contraceptive implant
options.B: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking
options.C: Standard male latex condoms
options.D: Combined oral contraceptive pills

question: A head nurse actively shares a successful handwashing checklist with three other wards through meetings and training. What is this action called?

options.B: Isolation
options.C: Diffusion
options.D: Regression

explanation: Spot on! Because the nurse made a deliberate, active effort to share the checklist, it is called spread.

question: Why do many developing countries often need external health support and international aid?

options.A: Private hospitals refuse to treat patients without foreign backing
options.B: International donors legally mandate that local taxes be abolished
options.C: Government health budgets often fall short of recommended funding targets
options.D: Citizens prefer foreign organizations over government clinics

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of a reservoir?

options.A: It is the natural habitat where pathogens live and multiply

question: An adult patient is overwhelmed by job loss and financial stress. Which nursing intervention best helps build resilience?

options.D: Telling the patient to ignore the stress because things always work out

question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.C: To prove that variable A causes a change in variable B
options.D: To compare two different patient groups after an intervention

explanation: Great job! Descriptive studies are all about painting a clear picture of what is going on right now, without needing to dig into the 'why' or 'how'.

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of health education in community nursing?

options.A: To empower individuals and groups to adopt healthy lifestyles
options.B: To diagnose complex medical disorders in hospital laboratories
options.C: To prescribe pharmaceutical drugs without a doctor's order
options.D: To generate revenue for local government health departments

question: What happens to complement protein levels (such as C3 and C4) in the blood during active serum sickness?

options.A: They decrease

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to open a patient's electronic health record?

options.C: During routine breaks to pass the time between shifts

question: Which part of the adolescent brain matures faster, leading to reward-seeking and impulsive behavior?

options.A: The limbic system

options.D: The brainstem

question: Which special pathways let electrical signals pass straight from one heart cell to the next?

question: Why are beta-blockers commonly prescribed for structural heart conditions?

options.B: To slow the heart rate and allow better ventricular filling time

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?

question: What is the main job of secondary lymphoid organs like lymph nodes?

options.C: They trap pathogens and provide a meeting place for mature immune cells.
options.D: They manufacture the primary hormones needed to regulate body temperature.

question: Why do esophageal varices develop in patients with portal hypertension?

question: When dealing with adolescent confidentiality dilemmas, what is the nurse's main responsibility?

question: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually take place?

question: What is the primary goal of Parent Management Training (PMT)?

question: What is your main nursing worry when a patient is given insulin for diabetes?

question: What is the medical term used when a stitched wound unexpectedly pops open?

question: Who does the WHO injection safety strategy aim to protect?

question: How does a community health nurse use epidemiological thinking during a clinic shift?

question: Why is it essential to use a pulse oximeter during a sedated endoscopy?

question: Even if a woman has received the HPV vaccine, why must she still go for regular cervical cancer screening later in life?

question: Why are standard gravity IV drips unreliable in a moving ambulance?

options.B: Plastic IV bags automatically dissolve when exposed to engine exhaust

question: What is the main purpose of a healthcare referral pathway?

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when trying to stop the spread of respiratory viruses in a hospital?

options.B: Ensuring proper room ventilation in clinical spaces
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before and after patient contact

question: What is a major advantage of recombinant human insulin compared to animal-sourced insulin?

question: Which of these questions shows great communication during a diet check-in?

question: How does economic empowerment directly help a person living with a physical disability?

question: Which secondary source uses math and statistics to combine the results of many different studies?

question: What is the document used by staff to track when medications are given to residents?

question: Which type of waste belongs in the black-colored hospital bin?

question: What is the big advantage of a concurrent audit compared to a retrospective one?

question: In healthcare, what does 'effectiveness' actually mean?

question: Why is a complete large bowel blockage considered a serious medical emergency?

question: During a follow-up assessment, what must a nurse always screen for directly?

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a secondary (acquired) immunodeficiency?

question: What is the employment status of a newly hired nurse who is still undergoing their initial probationary period?

question: Why do community health nurses look beyond just treating the individual patient sitting in front of them?

question: Why might a woman get a positive home pregnancy test even if she is not actually carrying a healthy pregnancy?

question: Which of these is NOT something food safety regulations normally check for?

options.A: Physical objects like metal shards or stones
options.B: Dangerous levels of chemical pesticide residues
options.C: Political views of the food manufacturing company owners
options.D: Harmful germs causing foodborne illnesses

explanation: Food safety is strictly about biological, chemical, and physical hazards—not who owns the company or what they believe!

question: What is the big benefit of using an inhaler instead of pills for an asthma patient?

options.A: It works within seconds to stop sudden bronchial muscle spasms completely
options.B: It delivers medication directly to lung tissue and reduces systemic side effects
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of developing oral fungal infections
options.D: It bypasses the liver entirely so the drug never enters the bloodstream

explanation: Inhalers send the drug right where the trouble is (the lungs), meaning less medicine floats around the rest of the body causing side effects.

question: What does a growing GDP fail to guarantee regarding a national health system?

options.A: That nurses will receive higher salaries
options.B: That the country will stop importing medications
options.C: That the wealth will automatically translate into better healthcare access
options.D: That hospitals will have electricity every day

explanation: Economic growth provides potential revenue, but political will and budget priorities dictate whether that money actually reaches clinics and patients.

question: What is the first-choice drug to prevent heavy bleeding (postpartum hemorrhage) right after delivery?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Calcium gluconate
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Ergometrine

explanation: Oxytocin is our superstar first-line defense because it works wonders on the uterus while being gentle on the heart.

question: Why might a nurse rush to handle a sudden disease outbreak over a common chronic illness?

options.A: The high severity and community panic demand immediate action
options.B: Outbreaks require no financial resources or planning
options.C: Government rules forbid treating long-term conditions
options.D: Chronic illnesses are impossible to treat in communities

explanation: Spot on! Sudden outbreaks spread fast and put lives in immediate danger, so they jump straight to the top of the priority list.

question: What is the main job of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine when given during shock?

options.A: Dissolving blood clots inside blocked arteries
options.B: Dilating peripheral airways to ease breathing
options.C: Lowering heart rate to reduce cardiac workload
options.D: Constricting blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors squeeze ('press') the blood vessels, tightening up the pipes to raise the blood pressure and keep vital organs perfused when the patient's own pressure is tanking.

question: What is a major benefit of connecting family caregivers to local support groups?

options.A: It helps reduce caregiver burnout by sharing coping strategies and emotional support.
options.B: It provides free prescription medications directly to the household.
options.C: It completely cures the neurodegenerative disease process in the patient.
options.D: It eliminates the need for professional physical and occupational therapy.

explanation: Looking after someone with a chronic illness is tough work. Support groups give families a safe space to vent, share tips, and remember they are not alone in the journey.

question: Which of these is a common reason why conflicts start in a hospital ward?

options.A: Ambiguous roles and unclear scopes of practice
options.B: Too many open nursing positions on the ward
options.C: An excess of available medical equipment
options.D: Identical personalities among all staff members

explanation: When people aren't quite sure where their duties end and someone else's begin, misunderstandings and friction are bound to happen.

question: Why is economic stability so important when a community health nurse tries to lower disease rates?

options.A: Economic status is the only factor recorded on a hospital admission form
options.B: Government policies prevent nurses from treating poor patients
options.C: Poverty often limits access to clean water, good food, and proper sanitation
options.D: Wealthy neighborhoods never experience infectious disease outbreaks

explanation: Well reasoned! When people have a stable income, they can easily afford basic needs like safe water and good nutrition, which naturally keeps diseases away.

question: What is the main job of the cerebrospinal fluid floating in the subarachnoid space?

options.A: To produce white blood cells for the nervous system
options.B: To anchor the spinal vertebrae to the spinal cord
options.C: To cushion the spinal cord against sudden physical shocks
options.D: To transmit electrical impulses directly to the muscles

explanation: Spot on! Cerebrospinal fluid acts like a built-in waterbed, protecting your delicate central nervous tissue from bumps and sudden movements.

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain gets flooded when someone takes addictive substances?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Dopamine is the brain's 'feel-good' chemical. Addictive drugs hijack this natural reward pathway, making the user crave more.

question: Which type of sexually transmitted infection can usually be cured with antibiotics?

options.A: Parasitic infections
options.B: Viral infections
options.C: Bacterial infections
options.D: Fungal infections

explanation: Bacterial STIs, like gonorrhea and chlamydia, can be knocked out easily with the right course of antibiotics.

question: Where in the gut does most iron absorption happen?

options.A: Transverse and descending colon
options.B: Cecum and appendix
options.C: Duodenum and upper jejunum
options.D: Stomach and lower esophagus

explanation: The upper part of the small intestine—specifically the duodenum and upper jejunum—is the main workstation where iron enters the bloodstream.

question: What substance protects the blood vessels inside the umbilical cord from getting squeezed flat?

options.A: Decidual tissue
options.B: Amniotic fluid
options.C: Chorionic villi
options.D: Wharton's jelly

explanation: Wharton's jelly is a soft, cushioned substance that acts like a built-in shock absorber for the baby's lifeline. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h3)

question: How do thyroid hormones affect a person's Basal Metabolic Rate?

options.A: They slow down heart rate to conserve oxygen inside the vital organs
options.B: They regulate water balance to prevent rapid shifts in body weight
options.C: They stimulate fat cells to store extra energy during periods of rest
options.D: They act as the main accelerator for cellular energy use across the body

explanation: Your thyroid gland is like the engine's spark plug. Its hormones control how fast your cells turn nutrients into energy, setting your overall metabolic pace.

question: How does music therapy help an agitated patient with dementia?

options.A: By physically restraining the patient during an episode
options.B: By teaching the patient how to play a complex musical instrument
options.C: By replacing all standard nursing observation duties
options.D: By evoking positive memories and decreasing behavioral agitation

explanation: Music speaks to deep emotional parts of the brain. When words fail, a familiar song can bring comfort and soothe a restless patient.

question: In patient safety design, what exactly is a 'forcing function'?

options.A: An oral warning given by supervisors after a near-miss event
options.B: A strict hospital rule punishing staff who forget documentation
options.C: A design feature that makes an incorrect action impossible to perform
options.D: A mandatory overtime shift assigned during staffing shortages

explanation: Think of a forcing function as a physical block against mistakes—like specialized tubing connectors that physically cannot be plugged into the wrong port.

question: Which of these skin conditions needs careful medical evaluation rather than just reassurance?

options.A: Mild palmar erythema on the hands
options.B: Linea nigra across the lower abdomen
options.C: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
options.D: Spider angiomas on the upper chest

explanation: While lines and spider veins are harmless, cholestasis involves the liver and requires close monitoring to keep the baby safe.

question: What is the main characteristic of a democratic leadership style?

options.A: Focus only on financial transactions
options.B: Shared decision-making and team input
options.C: Complete freedom given to junior staff
options.D: Strict rules with no room for discussion

explanation: Democratic leaders actively seek the opinions and ideas of their team members before making decisions. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses use screening tools like the CAGE questionnaire?

options.A: To measure the exact blood alcohol concentration
options.B: To diagnose clinical depression and anxiety
options.C: To test liver function enzymes in the blood
options.D: To quickly screen for potential alcohol use problems

explanation: Spot on! CAGE is a quick, easy set of questions that helps us spot clients who might be struggling with alcohol, so we can support them early.

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a quality improvement team?

options.A: Members feel safe speaking up without fear of punishment
options.B: All physical meeting rooms have secure electronic locks
options.C: Patient medical records remain strictly confidential
options.D: Staff members never experience physical fatigue at work

explanation: Exactly! When a team has psychological safety, staff feel comfortable sharing honest feedback and reporting mistakes without fear of being mocked or punished.

question: Which type of adverse event involves a patient picking up a brand new infection while admitted to the hospital?

options.A: Diagnostic failures
options.B: Medication-related events
options.C: Surgical complications
options.D: Healthcare-associated infections

explanation: Spot on! These are infections patients catch while staying in a health facility—like a catheter-related infection. Hand hygiene is our best weapon here!

question: Which Christian group often eats a plant-based diet and avoids pork?

options.A: Roman Catholics
options.B: Seventh-day Adventists
options.C: Pentecostal believers
options.D: Eastern Orthodox

explanation: Seventh-day Adventists often choose vegetarianism and avoid pork because they view the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit. You'll likely see this in clinical practice!

question: Why do community health clinics use safety boxes?

options.A: To keep surgical instruments sterile during rainy seasons
options.B: To separate paper trash from general food waste
options.C: To prevent needle-stick injuries and unsafe sharp disposal
options.D: To store expired medications safely away from children

explanation: Spot on! Puncture-proof safety boxes protect both healthcare workers and the local community from accidental needle sticks and blood infections.

question: Loud factory noise and extreme heat belong to which hazard category?

options.A: Psychosocial hazards
options.B: Ergonomic hazards
options.C: Physical hazards
options.D: Biological hazards

explanation: Physical hazards are environmental forces like noise, vibration, and extreme temperatures that interact directly with our bodies.

question: How would you best describe a skin macule?

options.A: A solid, elevated lump deep in the skin
options.B: A fluid-filled blister larger than one centimeter
options.C: A flat, unraised change in skin color
options.D: A raised, hard plateau made of merged bumps

explanation: A macule is completely flat. You can't feel it by running your finger over it—it's simply a change in color, like a freckle.

question: What action should a midwife take immediately when an unpredictable obstetric emergency occurs at a primary care clinic?

options.A: Perform a major surgical procedure in the clinic
options.B: Stabilize the patient and initiate a prompt, organized referral
options.C: Discharge the patient home with instructions to rest
options.D: Wait for the patient's family to raise funds before doing anything

explanation: The midwife must stabilize critical vitals and quickly transfer the patient to a facility equipped for higher-level care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h6)

question: Where does peripheral fatigue mainly start in the body?

options.A: Along the main pathways of the spinal cord
options.B: Inside the cerebral cortex of the brain
options.C: Within the muscle fibers or neuromuscular junction
options.D: Through systemic inflammatory cytokines in the blood

explanation: You've got this! Peripheral fatigue happens right at the muscles and the junctions where nerves meet them. Even though your brain sends the signal to move, the muscles themselves are just too worn out to respond properly.

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To allow rapid absorption of testosterone directly into the skin
options.B: To keep the testicles cooler than body temperature for sperm production
options.C: To provide a direct connection to the external urinary meatus
options.D: To protect the reproductive organs from high intra-abdominal pressure

explanation: Sperm are sensitive! They need a slightly cooler temperature than the rest of the body to grow and develop properly, which is why the scrotum hangs outside.

question: Your nursing team tries a new handover checklist, but the run chart shows no improvement after two weeks. What should you do next?

options.A: Punish the night shift nurses for failing to follow the new rules
options.B: Stop collecting data entirely and pretend the intervention succeeded
options.C: Treat the result as valuable learning to adapt the checklist for another cycle
options.D: Fire the nurse manager and hire an outside corporate consultant

explanation: Don't worry! In nursing quality improvement, a trial that doesn't work right away is just helpful feedback to guide your next try.

question: Why does a tracheostomy tube have a removable inner cannula?

options.A: It allows easy cleaning and removal of dried mucus

options.C: It measures the exact pressure in the lungs
options.D: It allows the patient to talk without a valve

explanation: Mucus builds up fast! The inner cannula can be easily taken out and cleaned so the airway stays open and clear.

question: What makes the blood-brain barrier so tough for most drugs to cross?

options.A: Tightly joined capillary cells with no large pores
options.B: A thick outer layer of skull bone
options.C: Constant high-speed blood flow that washes drugs away
options.D: Enzymes in the blood that destroy drugs instantly

explanation: Unlike regular blood vessels that have tiny spaces for things to slip through, brain capillaries are locked together tightly to protect the brain.

question: Why can cultural beliefs and stigma create obstacles during problem identification?

options.A: Stigma forces communities to build private hospitals for themselves
options.B: Local customs automatically cure all infectious diseases without treatment
options.C: Residents may hide health issues or distrust outside health workers
options.D: Traditional rulers refuse to let nurses keep written records

explanation: Fear of stigma and lack of trust in outsiders can prevent community members from sharing true health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)

question: When is the best time of day to collect a sputum (phlegm) sample?

options.A: Just before the patient goes to sleep at night
options.B: Right after the patient takes a warm shower
options.C: Immediately after a heavy lunch or dinner meal
options.D: Early in the morning before eating or drinking

explanation: Secretions pool in the airways overnight, making early morning the absolute best time to catch a good deep cough sample.

question: About how long are the intestines in an adult human body when fully stretched out?

options.A: Fifteen meters
options.B: Two meters
options.C: Nine meters
options.D: One meter

question: What do we mean by the "psychosocial impact" of an emergency?

options.A: The financial cost of rebuilding a damaged hospital
options.B: The physical injuries sustained during a natural disaster
options.C: How external events affect emotional and social well-being
options.D: Biological changes caused strictly by physical infection

question: Which instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding pelvic rest after an MVA?

options.C: Exercise strenuously starting the very next morning

question: Which of these is an example of disaster 'mitigation'?

options.A: Treating injured survivors in a hospital emergency room

options.C: Enforcing building codes in flood-prone areas
options.D: Distributing blankets to displaced families in a camp

question: Why shouldn't you rush or speed too much when transporting an accident victim?

options.A: Vehicles consume too much fuel when driven too fast
options.B: Rushing can compromise the airway or worsen existing injuries
options.C: Hospitals prefer patients to arrive slowly for administrative reasons
options.D: Rescuers get too tired to document the incident properly

question: A nurse cares for an immobile surgery patient who is showing poor wound healing and muscle wasting. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Inadequate nutritional intake failing to meet elevated metabolic demands

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical practice when presenting qualitative research results?

options.A: Revealing the real names of participants to give them credit

options.C: Separating factual results from personal opinions

question: What is the best way for a nurse to teach a client how to use a condom properly?

question: What is an epithelial tissue made of just a single layer of cells called?

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when scaling up a quality improvement project?

question: What do we mean by a 'food desert' in a community?

options.B: A supermarket that refuses to sell bottled drinking water

options.D: A local restaurant that only serves dry baked goods

question: Why is checking a patient's current medications so important during a sexual health assessment?

options.A: Many common drugs cause sexual side effects

question: When we talk about 'somatosensation', what kind of feelings are we including?

question: What tells you right away that your needle has successfully entered the vein?

question: Why is it important to encourage a labouring mum to empty her bladder regularly?

options.B: To stop Braxton Hicks contractions from returning

question: Why should nursing researchers care about national and global health goals?

options.A: It helps secure research funding and ensures the study addresses urgent needs

question: When deciding on a study design, which of these is completely irrelevant?

question: Why is prevalence data most useful for community health nurses?

options.D: It helps plan long-term care and allocate resources

question: Why can keeping patient information private be tricky in a home setting?

options.A: Patients demand that all their lab results be broadcasted

question: Why is it crucial to quickly report abnormal vital signs to the doctor?

options.C: It allows the healthcare team to intervene before the patient's condition worsens

question: What is the final step in the core disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Collecting more patient samples

options.D: Taking public health action

explanation: Data collection and analysis are useless unless they lead directly to meaningful public health action and control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What should you do immediately when a pregnant woman starts having an eclamptic seizure?

options.A: Hold her arms and legs tightly straight to stop the shaking
options.B: Force a wooden spatula between her teeth to hold the airway open

question: What type of exercise is especially great for helping men fight off muscle loss during andropause?

options.A: Breathing exercises

options.D: Resistance training

question: Why should a patient with uncontrolled epilepsy wear a medical alert bracelet?

options.D: To ensure bystanders and emergency workers know what is wrong

explanation: If a patient can't speak for themselves after a fit, that little bracelet does the talking for them, making sure helpers know exactly what condition they have.

question: Which part of the reflex arc carries the electrical signal away from the spinal cord to the target muscle or gland?

options.A: Integration center

options.D: Motor neuron

question: How do qualitative researchers usually find key insights in interview texts?

question: Why must a nurse check skin sensation below the level of a spinal cord injury?

question: Why should nurses use a friendly, non-judgmental tone when asking patients about drug use?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from malpractice suits
options.B: It encourages patients to provide honest health disclosures
options.C: It ensures the doctor prescribes higher drug doses
options.D: It prevents the patient from staying in the hospital

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from moral blame, they are much more honest about their health history. Great nursing care starts with empathy!

question: Why can checking a patient's blood composition tell us so much about their overall health?

options.C: Blood cells are the largest cells in the human body and easily visible under basic light
options.D: Blood is the only fluid in the body that contains water and dissolved electrolytes

question: Why is boosting domestic revenue (like local taxes and insurance) so important for a sustainable healthcare system?

options.A: It reduces heavy reliance on unpredictable foreign donor funds and loans

options.C: It stops patients from visiting hospitals for routine checkups

explanation: Building internal financial strength gives a country independence, ensuring its health sector stays steady even if foreign grants change.

question: Which brain structure acts as the main relay station for sensory messages heading to the cortex?

options.A: Cerebellum

options.D: Thalamus

question: What is the biggest perk of long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like IUDs?

explanation: LARCs are super convenient because once they are in place, the client does not have to remember a daily pill.

question: When helping a Nigerian patient plan a healthy, balanced local diet, which food combination is best?

question: Why is understanding the family life cycle important for a community health nurse?

options.D: It allows you to calculate household income

explanation: Every life stage has its own unique health risks, helping you know what guidance or preventive care to offer next.

question: The government decides to drop plans for a luxury VIP ward and instead buys thousands of mosquito nets for villages. What does this show?

options.D: Horizontal equity

question: Why do TB patients have to take a combination of multiple drugs instead of just one?

question: What is a major goal of any good pharmacovigilance program?

options.D: Replacing traditional clinical trials with computer simulations

question: You just removed a dirty dressing from a draining wound while wearing gloves. What is your immediate next step after taking them off?
