options.C: Perform hand hygiene immediately
options.D: Write the nursing notes in the chart

explanation: Always clean your hands right after taking off gloves! Microbes can easily slip through tiny, unseen tears in gloves, so hand hygiene seals the deal.

question: When you swallow a pill, where does it start undergoing metabolism before it even reaches the rest of the body?

options.A: Bone marrow and lymph nodes
options.B: Intestinal wall and liver
options.C: Heart and skeletal muscles
options.D: Spleen and pancreas

explanation: Before an oral drug gets into general circulation, it has to pass through the gut wall and take a trip right through the liver, where a good portion of it gets broken down first.

question: What was the main focus of nursing studies during the early part of the twentieth century?

options.A: Hospital staffing and nursing education
options.B: Molecular genetics and cellular biology
options.C: Pharmacological drug trials
options.D: Advanced surgical techniques

explanation: Early research mostly looked at how to organize nursing schools, manage hospital routines, and assign student workloads efficiently. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is mixed feeding (breast milk plus other foods or water) discouraged for infants exposed to HIV?

options.A: It damages the infant's immature gut lining and increases transmission risk.
options.B: It is too expensive for families living in rural communities.
options.C: It prevents the baby from ever developing taste preferences.
options.D: It causes immediate allergic reactions in all newborn infants.

explanation: Introducing other liquids or foods irritates the baby's gut wall, making it much easier for the HIV virus in breast milk to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: Why do we need different sectors—like health, law enforcement, and social services—to work together when managing violence cases?

options.A: Because police officers must approve all nursing care plans
options.B: Because survivors need medical, legal, social, and psychological support
options.C: Because hospital nurses have the legal power to arrest criminals
options.D: Because social workers are the only ones allowed to treat physical injuries

explanation: Spot on! No single profession can fix every problem a violence survivor faces. Teamwork across health, law, and social services is essential.

question: A young teenager is diagnosed with a rare ovarian tumor that starts from the cells that make eggs. What type of tumor is this?

options.A: Germ cell tumor
options.B: Stromal tumor
options.C: Squamous cell tumor
options.D: Epithelial tumor

explanation: Great thinking! Germ cell tumors arise from the egg-producing cells and are more commonly seen in younger patients.

question: What serious long-term problem can happen if severe, chronic anaemia is ignored?

options.A: Heart failure
options.B: Bone softening
options.C: Liver cirrhosis
options.D: Kidney stones

explanation: If the heart is forced to pump extra fast for months or years to move oxygen-poor blood, the heart muscle eventually gets exhausted and begins to fail.

question: During a clinic visit, what sign might make a nurse suspect a young patient is in an early marriage?

options.A: Refusing to answer any questions about her medical history
options.B: Demanding to see the head doctor without family present
options.C: Expressing high levels of satisfaction with her home life
options.D: Hesitation to speak when an older partner answers for her

explanation: A young minor in a forced early union often acts very quiet or lets her older spouse control the entire conversation.

question: Which of these is NOT a common trigger for a psychotic episode?

options.A: Using recreational cannabis
options.B: Experiencing severe life stress
options.C: Having a family history of psychosis
options.D: Eating a high-sodium diet

explanation: Spot on! Eating salty food won't cause psychosis, but heavy stress, genetics, and substances like cannabis definitely can.

question: Which level of prevention covers routine childhood immunizations?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Well done! Primary prevention is all about stopping the disease before it even starts—just like vaccines do.

question: What is a common mistake nurses should avoid when assessing patients during a disaster?

options.A: Spending too much time on detailed checks for one stable patient
options.B: Applying pressure bandages immediately to actively bleeding wounds
options.C: Checking vital signs and airway status before administering any drugs
options.D: Prioritizing patients tagged red before addressing walking wounded

explanation: In a mass casualty setting, spending all your time on one stable patient means others who are critical might miss out on care.

question: You notice a care assistant rushing an elderly resident through a meal. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Educate the assistant on patient-centered feeding techniques and safety
options.B: Report the assistant to the police for physical abuse immediately
options.C: Ignore the incident since assistants are trained separately
options.D: Take over feeding all residents in the facility personally

explanation: Well done! As a nurse, you supervise support staff. Teaching them the right, gentle way to feed residents ensures safe and dignified care.

question: What is the immediate next step after a school nurse identifies a health defect during a screening?

options.A: Providing a prompt referral for further clinical care
options.B: Keeping the finding secret from the parents
options.C: Prescribing specialized medicines immediately
options.D: Expelling the student from the school system

explanation: Screening is only useful if followed by a referral so the child can receive proper diagnosis and treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h7)

question: A nurse teaches villagers to boil their drinking water to stop cholera. Which part of the disease chain is this targeting?

options.A: The genetic makeup of the host
options.B: The incubation period of the germ
options.C: The vehicle of transmission
options.D: The virulence of the pathogen

explanation: Water acts as the 'vehicle' carrying the germ to people. Boiling it breaks the chain right there. Brilliant public health nursing!

question: What does drug efficacy refer to?

options.A: The exact cost of the pharmaceutical item
options.B: The maximum response a drug can produce
options.C: The chemical stability of the drug bottle
options.D: The speed of absorption through the gut

explanation: Efficacy is the highest peak of relief or healing that a medication can possibly deliver for your patient.

question: Why must rescue workers stabilize a victim before moving them to a hospital?

options.A: To address life-threatening injuries and prevent deterioration during transport
options.B: To ensure the rescue team gets enough rest before the next mission
options.C: To reduce the total paperwork required by the receiving hospital staff
options.D: To identify the personal belongings and insurance status of the patient

explanation: Brilliant! Stabilizing stops immediate threats like severe bleeding so the patient can survive the bumpy journey to the hospital.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing healthcare collaboration in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant medical supplies and excessive staffing levels
options.B: Inadequate infrastructure and fragmented record-keeping systems
options.C: Deep-seated professional hierarchies and historical power imbalances
options.D: Inter-professional rivalry between different healthcare worker groups

explanation: Correct! Nigeria's healthcare system unfortunately battles with shortages, not an excess of staff or medical supplies.

question: Why does chronic kidney disease often lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Urine output drops so low that calcium crystallizes inside the bladder.
options.B: Failing kidneys cannot activate vitamin D or clear phosphate properly.
options.C: The kidneys start producing parathyroid hormone in place of the glands.
options.D: Renal failure directly destroys all four parathyroid glands within weeks.

explanation: When kidneys fail, they struggle to clear phosphate and activate vitamin D, which drops your calcium levels and forces the parathyroid glands to work overtime.

question: Why does a nurse use the back of the hand when checking skin temperature over a swollen joint?

options.A: It is required by standard infection control guidelines for wound care
options.B: The skin on the dorsal hand is thinner and more sensitive to temperature changes
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling intimidated by a direct palm touch
options.D: The palm is too warm to detect minor differences in body heat

explanation: The thin skin on the back of the hand is much better at detecting subtle variations in local skin warmth. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are administrative decisions much better when they are backed by nursing research?

options.A: It guarantees that the hospital will never face any lawsuits
options.B: It balances financial costs with patient safety and staff efficiency
options.C: It reduces the salaries of senior nursing management
options.D: It allows administrators to ignore staff complaints completely

explanation: Well done! Research helps managers make smart financial choices while still keeping patients safe and nurses supported.

question: How does poor transport infrastructure affect infectious disease surveillance?

options.A: It prevents nurses from washing their hands properly
options.B: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions on paper
options.C: It forces patients to walk to international hospitals
options.D: It delays getting biological samples safely to testing laboratories

explanation: Without good roads or transport, samples take too long to reach labs, slowing down outbreak detection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is a vital nursing duty right after giving an antidote to a poisoned patient?

options.A: Stopping all cardiac monitoring to let the patient rest
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately if they feel better
options.C: Restricting all oral fluids for the next 48 hours
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for secondary complications

explanation: You're doing great! Antidotes can sometimes wear off before the poison is completely gone from the body, so close monitoring of vital signs is a must to keep the patient safe.

question: What is the main reason we advise patients with high blood pressure to cut down on salt (sodium)?

options.A: To prevent the rapid digestion of dietary carbohydrates
options.B: To reduce intravascular volume and vascular resistance
options.C: To increase total body serum potassium levels
options.D: To stimulate increased red blood cell production

explanation: Salt makes the body hold onto water. Less salt means less fluid volume in the blood vessels, which lowers the pressure pushing against their walls. Easy and logical!

question: What is the primary maternal health benefit of properly spacing pregnancies?

options.A: Permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles
options.B: Eliminating the need for any antenatal care visits
options.C: Giving the mother's body time to recover physically
options.D: Ensuring the mother gives birth only to male children

explanation: Proper spacing allows a woman's body to restore vital nutrients like iron and heal from the physical stress of a previous pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: What is a major downside of using online questionnaires for hospital patients?

options.A: They prevent researchers from collecting any numerical data
options.B: They force patients to answer every question before submitting
options.C: They always cost significantly more than printed paper surveys
options.D: They may exclude patients who lack internet access or devices

explanation: The digital divide means older or lower-income patients might not have the technology required to complete online forms. Excellent real-world nursing perspective!

question: What simple advice can you give a patient who complains of a dry mouth from their medication?

options.A: Apply petroleum jelly directly to the tongue
options.B: Drink at least five liters of water every hour
options.C: Stop taking the medication immediately
options.D: Suck on hard candies or chew sugarless gum

explanation: Brilliant! Hard candies and sugarless gum safely kickstart saliva flow and make the dry mouth much easier to handle.

question: How do antibiotics used in agriculture often end up in humans?

options.A: Through the food chain from livestock consumption
options.B: By drinking purified bottled water from wells
options.C: Through direct injection of vaccines in schools
options.D: By airborne dust blowing directly into city hospitals

explanation: When farm animals are given antibiotics, resistant germs can develop in them and pass on to humans through meat handling or consumption.

question: What is the main goal of evaluating healthcare objectives?

options.A: To understand barriers and adapt strategies for better patient care.
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for nurses.
options.C: To justify cutting the budget of underperforming units.
options.D: To find staff members to blame when targets are missed.

explanation: Evaluation isn't about blaming people; it's about figuring out what roadblocks got in the way so we can improve patient care next time.

question: What is the main goal of a health insurance scheme?

options.A: To pool financial risks and protect people from high out-of-pocket costs
options.B: To ensure that doctors receive higher salaries than other workers
options.C: To provide free luxury accommodation for all hospitalized patients
options.D: To eliminate the need for government funding in hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Insurance pools money from many people so that when someone falls sick, they don't get completely wiped out financially by medical bills.

question: What is the primary function of cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: To transmit electrical signals across synapses
options.B: To cushion the brain and provide nutritional support
options.C: To produce red blood cells for nervous tissue
options.D: To cool down the body during a high fever

explanation: CSF acts as a shock-absorbing liquid cushion while also nourishing the central nervous system tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why does maternal hyperglycemia lead to macrosomia in the developing fetus?

options.A: Excess amniotic fluid stretches the fetal bones
options.B: Maternal fat deposits transfer directly to the baby
options.C: High fetal insulin acts as a growth promoter
options.D: The placenta grows larger to absorb extra water

explanation: Excess glucose from the mother triggers the baby to make too much insulin, and insulin acts like a growth hormone that causes the baby to grow unusually large. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h3)

question: Why does good teamwork improve a patient's transition from the hospital to home?

options.A: Different team members coordinate discharge education and resources smoothly
options.B: Doctors make all final decisions without consulting family members
options.C: Patients are discharged much faster without receiving any medications
options.D: Nurses take over all financial responsibilities for the household

explanation: You nailed it! Smooth teamwork ensures that when a patient is ready to go home, everyone (nurses, doctors, pharmacists, social workers) is on the same page.

question: What kind of data do we usually analyze using a Chi-Square test?

options.A: Ratio level measurements
options.B: Paired interval scores
options.C: Continuous numerical data
options.D: Categorical data

explanation: You've got this! A Chi-Square test is used for data that falls into distinct groups or categories (like male/female or yes/no), rather than numbers on a continuous scale.

question: Why is evaluation considered an essential final step in the directing process?

options.A: It helps managers spot problems and adjust their approach for better care
options.B: It is required by law to punish nurses who make mistakes on duty
options.C: It proves to the hospital board that the manager is working hard
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any future shift planning

explanation: Continuous evaluation provides the feedback loop needed to refine leadership strategies and protect patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h8)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to communicate when talking with a teenager client?

options.A: Speak loudly and use complex Latin terms
options.B: Use simple language without complicated medical jargon
options.C: Write everything down without speaking directly
options.D: Ask parents to answer all questions on behalf of the youth

explanation: Keep it simple and clear! Avoiding heavy medical jargon helps young clients understand their health without feeling intimidated.

question: What crucial advice should you give a patient prescribed a course of antibiotics?

options.A: Complete the entire course even if symptoms disappear early
options.B: Stop taking the pills immediately when fever subsides
options.C: Double the next dose if you forget to take one on time
options.D: Share leftover medicine with family members who feel sick

explanation: Always finish the prescription! Stopping early lets the strongest bacteria survive and bounce back stronger than before.

question: What is the main difference between a vaccine contraindication and a precaution?

options.A: A contraindication allows live vaccines, while a precaution requires immediate quarantine.
options.B: A contraindication is a mild fever, while a precaution is always a permanent physical disability.
options.C: A contraindication means the vaccine is unsafe, while a precaution means it should be delayed or used with caution.
options.D: A contraindication only applies to adults, while a precaution applies exclusively to newborn infants.

explanation: Spot on! A contraindication means 'Stop, this is unsafe here,' while a precaution means 'Proceed with caution or wait a little bit.'

question: Which of these is NOT a direct complication of an unsafe or incomplete abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Intrauterine adhesions
options.C: Severe pelvic infection
options.D: Heavy hemorrhage

explanation: Gestational diabetes is linked to metabolic changes during an ongoing pregnancy, whereas bleeding, infection, and adhesions follow abortion complications.
